newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Growers calm about dryness in Brazil soybean area.
newsitem.headline: Growers calm about dryness in Brazil soybean area.

text.p: Areas of Brazil's key soybean growing region of Rio Grande do Sul were becoming dry after 10 days without rain but a cold front was forecast to bring fresh showers on January 30, independent meteorologist Somar said.
Growers said the problem was not yet serious enough to cause fears of a drop in the crop.
"On Thursday rains are forecast in the producing region of Rio Grande do Sul due to the entry of a new cold front," Somar said in a weekly report.
"This system arrives in the south of Brazil, with moderate activity, causing rains of around 30 mm and alleviating the dryness which is affecting the region," the report added.
The driest regions were Cruz Alta, Panambi and Sao Luiz Gonzaga in Rio Grande do Sul and parts of the east of Santa Catarina, meteorologist Marcos Massari told Reuters.
Growers said scattered showers had fallen since widespread rains 10 days ago, but there were pockets of dryness.
"It's isolated spots," said Eloi Hilgert at the Rio Grande do Sul agricultural secretariat. "There's no indication of any crop loss yet."
But he added, "If we don't get generalised rains in the next 10 days, then we will have a problem."
The weather remained cloudy with scattered showers in Parana, where rainfall has exceeded 100 mm in the last week, Massari said.
